patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of persistent fatigue and several episodes of lower abdominal pain. Despite being on sick leave for 2 weeks, symptoms have not improved. She expresses a concern that she might have cancer and requests a diagnostic laparoscopy. She was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months prior, currently taking omeprazole.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Works as a nurse, has been under a lot of stress at work.

Review_of_Systems.Skin: Numerous crusts along the left arm veins
Review_of_Systems.Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur along the right-upper sternal border
Review_of_Systems.Musculoskeletal: Generalized weakness of the proximal muscles

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with fatigue, episodes of lower abdominal pain, and a self-stated high cancer concern.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hi doctor—I'm a 26-year-old nurse, and for the last two months I've had persistent fatigue and I’ve been noticing paleness. I’ve also had a few episodes of lower abdominal pain, and despite being off work for two weeks my symptoms haven’t improved; with all the stress lately, I’m worried it could be something serious like cancer.”

turns.doctor_question: I'm sorry to hear you're not feeling well. To help me better understand what you're experiencing, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as blurriness, dark spots, or any loss of sight?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any changes in my vision like blurriness, dark spots, or any loss of sight. Mostly it’s the persistent fatigue and the episodes of lower abdominal pain that are worrying me.”

turns.doctor_question: To help me get a better picture of your overall health, could you tell me if you currently smoke or have a history of smoking?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I don’t smoke and I’ve never had a history of smoking.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of how you're feeling, have you been experiencing any nausea or feeling sick to your stomach lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t really had nausea or been vomiting—my main issues are the ongoing fatigue with episodes of lower abdominal pain. I do feel very run-down and stressed, and my mood has been a bit down because it’s not improving.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your health, have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breast area that do not cause you any pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breast area, and nothing there is painful. My main concern is still the ongoing fatigue and the intermittent lower abdominal pain, and I’m just feeling very worried with everything not getting better.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your current health, have you noticed any changes in the color of your urine, such as it appearing darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—my urine color hasn’t changed noticeably; it hasn’t been darker than usual. It’s mainly the persistent fatigue with intermittent lower abdominal pain, plus I’ve been feeling very run-down and worried.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand that finding a change in your breast can be concerning. To help me better understand what you are experiencing, could you tell me if you have noticed this breast mass growing or changing in size rapidly over a short period of time?
turns.patient_answer: “No doctor, I haven’t noticed any breast lumps or any change in size at all—nothing seems to be growing or changing rapidly. My concern is mainly the persistent fatigue and the intermittent lower abdominal pain that hasn’t improved even though I’ve been off work.”

turns.doctor_question: I'm sorry to hear you're not feeling well. To help me better understand what might be going on, could you tell me if you have been experiencing any pain in your wrist?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t had any pain in my wrist. My symptoms are mainly persistent fatigue and intermittent lower abdominal pain, and I’ve also felt very pale and weak, which is why I’m concerned.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a clearer picture of what you're experiencing, could you please tell me if you have noticed any skin lesions, rashes, or unusual marks running along the veins of your arms?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes doctor, I have noticed numerous crusts along the veins on my left arm, which look like unusual marks. I haven’t had any widespread rash elsewhere, but those changes have been worrying me.”

turns.doctor_question: I understand. To help me get a better picture of your health, I’d like to ask about your breathing: Do you find that you experience shortness of breath or difficulty catching your breath when you are physically active, such as walking or climbing stairs?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t really noticed shortness of breath with walking or climbing stairs. It’s mainly the persistent fatigue with the episodes of lower abdominal pain, along with the paleness and those crusts along the veins on my left arm.”

turns.doctor_question: To help me get a clearer picture of your health, could you tell me if you have used any recreational or non-prescribed drugs recently?
turns.patient_answer: “No doctor, I haven’t used any recreational or non-prescribed drugs recently. I’m only taking omeprazole for my peptic ulcer disease, and otherwise I haven’t changed anything.”
